summary: A 1928 Aermotor LS-40 moved from Alander Mountain to Washburn and then Beebe Hill; operated until 1987, registered 1997, and recently restored.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 tower, 60 ft as first erected

staffing.status: closed as a lookout in 1987; no current staffing reported

access.note: NYSDEC forest page describes the fire tower as open to the public; Wikipedia reported it deemed unsafe as of late 2024. Check NYSDEC before climbing.

visit.trail_note: Reached on the multiple-use trails of the Beebe Hill and Harvey Mountain state forests from parking areas; a public lean-to sits just off the summit along the main trail.

events.note: Aermotor LS-40 60-foot tower erected on Alander Mountain by the Taconic State Park Commission, just inside Massachusetts, to detect fires on park land

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates the helicopter move to November 1963; Wikipedia gives 1964. The record uses 1963 from the NHLR, which has the detailed account, and the story notes the Wikipedia date.

Wikipedia says the state forest website deemed the tower unsafe as of late 2024. The NYSDEC forest page describes a fire tower open to the public, and the NHLR reports a recent restoration as of 2025. The story reports the disagreement and gives the newer sources the weight of the current status.

notes_for_editor: The tower's history is well documented in the NHLR detail page, which the record cites. The planned NHLR history PDF (2966), chapter PDFs (2962, 2963) and beebehill.info all failed (404 or DNS), so their content is not used. Relocation year conflicts: NHLR gives November 1963 for the move to Beebe Hill and Wikipedia gives 1964; a web search summary also mentioned a 1932 versus 1933 Washburn re-erection and a 1988 end-of-season closure with a 1989 official closure, but those came from search snippets and were not read on a fetched page, so they are not in the story. Current status is the main open question: Wikipedia (late 2024, unsafe) versus NYSDEC page (open to the public) and NHLR (restored 2025). Verify on site or with NYSDEC before any climb. Access level is public for hiking the forest; climbability of the tower itself is not established and is left unset. The NHLR notes the tower was Aermotor LS-40 60-foot as first erected, not necessarily its current height.
